html:
A battle fought about 1274 BCE by the Orontes River near the city of Kadesh in western Syria, between the Egyptian army of Ramesses II and the Hittite army of Muwatalli II. It is the earliest battle whose tactics and numbers are known in detail, and probably the largest chariot battle ever fought.

The two empires were fighting for control of Syria. Ramesses, misled by false reports that the Hittites were far away, marched ahead with part of his army. The Hittite chariots struck his camp by surprise. Ramesses rallied his men and the arrival of fresh troops saved him, but he did not take Kadesh.

Neither side won outright. Ramesses carved his own version of a great victory on temples at Abydos, Karnak, Luxor and Abu Simbel. The real outcome came later: in about 1259 BCE Ramesses and the Hittite king Hattusili III made the Egyptian Hittite peace treaty, the earliest peace treaty whose text survives in both parties' versions.
